gloss: to be moved to tears; to get teary-eyed

definitions.gloss: to be moved to tears; to get teary-eyed; to well up with tears
definitions.explanation: To have tears form in one's eyes without necessarily crying. Describes the moment when emotion causes tears to well up, whether from sadness, joy, or being deeply moved.

examples.japanese: {感動|かんどう}して{涙|なみだ}ぐんだ。
examples.english: I was moved and got teary-eyed.

examples.japanese: {卒業式|そつぎょうしき}で{先生|せんせい}が{涙|なみだ}ぐんでいた。
examples.english: The teacher was getting teary-eyed at the graduation ceremony.

examples.japanese: {久|ひさ}しぶりに{再会|さいかい}した{友人|ゆうじん}の{姿|すがた}を{見|み}て、{思|おも}わず{涙|なみだ}ぐんでしまった。
examples.english: Seeing a friend I hadn't met in a long time, I couldn't help but well up with tears.

notes:
Describes the state just before actual crying — tears forming in the eyes. More restrained than {泣|な}く (to cry).

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
- {感動|かんどう}して{涙|なみだ}ぐむ (to be moved to tears)
- {思|おも}わず{涙|なみだ}ぐむ (to involuntarily get teary-eyed)
- {涙|なみだ}ぐむ{声|こえ} (a voice choked with tears)

USAGE NOTE:
{涙|なみだ}ぐむ is intransitive and focuses on the involuntary emotional response of tears welling up. It is more literary and expressive than simply saying {涙|なみだ}が{出|で}る (tears come out).
